learning_outcomes.text: Be familiar with the basic concepts of structured programming and be able to develop and implement simple algorithms in Python.
Be prepared to attend the computational courses of the curriculum: Advanced Computer Programming (ETY-413), as well as classes that need programming skills.
Be able to understand and develop codes in programming languages like Python.
Have gained expertise in tackling a complex problem by analysing it into many, simple, and easy tasks.
Use of libraries and multiple bibliographic sources
Search for resources and online lessons
Create notes and stand-alone study method

syllabus_topics: Python (v. 3.10+) installation, Interactive environment, code execution from command line.
Objects, Variables, Numerical operators, Expressions, Coding rules, Modules.
Numerical types (Integer, Float, Complex), Boolean type, Type casting, Printing, Printing formatting, Interactive input.
Basic built-in functions (abs(), len(), range(), list(), min(), max(), etc.), Module importing, Mathematical functions of math module.
Control commands (if…elif…else and match…case), Comparison operators, Boolean operators, Membership operators, Identity operators, Boolean expressions.
Looping commands (while…else, for…else), Flow change commands (break, continue, pass).
User defined functions, Arguments, Default arguments.
Mutable objects: Lists (Append - Delete list elements, Slicing).
teaching_methods: Communication through course website and email
Material posted on asynchronous training platform
assessment_rules: Students are examined through a series of tests every week and at the end of the semester. Student evaluation is specifically defined.
